ops.statement: In this sandbox the `py` first on PATH is a codex-runtime Python 3.12 shim at C:/Users/fredc/.local/bin/py that LACKS project deps (fastf1/sklearn) -- it fails to even collect the test suite (root conftest.py imports deps). The REAL project launcher is Python 3.14 and is reachable as C:/Users/fredc/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WindowsApps/py.exe (or the interpreter directly at C:/Users/fredc/AppData/Local/Python/pythoncore-3.14-64/python.exe). This shadows silently: an engine `command` postcondition of the form `py -m pytest ...` runs in the engine's POSIX subshell which inherits the caller's PATH, so it resolves to the 3.12 shim and FALSELY FAILS collection unless the caller PREPENDS `export PATH="/c/Users/fredc/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WindowsApps:$PATH"` in the same shell as the `advance`. Every crew (2 impl + 2 review) and the commander's own re-verification hit this; the fix is a PATH prepend (or invoking the 3.14 python.exe by absolute path). Handoffs must state the PATH-prep line up front; the engine advance that runs a `py` command postcondition must be issued with the prepend.
ops.grounding: epic659-661: G1 implementer RESULT + G1/G2 reviewer RESULTs all independently flagged the 3.12-shim-lacking-deps / real-3.14-at-WindowsApps discovery; the commander confirmed `py --version`=3.12.13 via the Bash tool vs 3.14.3 via WindowsApps/py.exe, and had to prepend WindowsApps to PATH on both g1-integrate and g2-integrate advances so the frozen `py -m pytest` command postconditions resolved to 3.14 and passed (they would otherwise fail collection).
ops.bank_reason: First observation in this sandbox environment -- re-observe whether the same shim-shadowing recurs on the next delegated commander run here (a persistent sandbox property) vs a one-off of this machine's PATH ordering, before deciding the fix is a standing launch-order/handoff boilerplate line, a run_crew.py/engine PATH-normalization, or just this run's environment quirk. If it recurs, the engine command-postcondition mechanism silently resolving `py` to a deps-less shim is a real cross-run trap worth an upstream fix (e.g. the engine or run_crew resolving a project-configured interpreter rather than bare `py`).
